description: This section of the Report on Government Services is the standard annual comparison of fire and emergency services across the Australian states and territories, covering what they cost, how many people they employ, how many incidents they attend and how quickly they respond. It is compiled by the Productivity Commission for the intergovernmental Steering Committee for the Review of Government Service Provision, from data supplied by state and territory fire, rescue and State Emergency Service agencies. The 2026 edition, released in February 2026, reports series from as early as 1995 up to 2024-25 for each state and territory and Australia. Measures include revenue and expenditure, paid and volunteer staff, fires and other incidents attended, State Emergency Service incidents and hours, response times to structure fires, residential fires and smoke alarm status, confinement of fires, deaths, hospital admissions for fire injuries and weather-related injuries, and asset losses. The data are available free under a Creative Commons licence, as a download of a long-format CSV dataset and Excel data tables. Caveats: agency structures and counting rules differ between jurisdictions, so the footnotes matter, and figures are aggregated to state level. Simulation uses: setting response time distributions, incident rates and resourcing levels for fire and emergency service capacity models, and comparing jurisdictions. Related records: CFA emergency response times (data-cfa-emergency-response-times) and Ambulance Victoria statistics (data-ambulance-victoria-incident-statistics) give finer Victorian detail.
